english.title: Aid / abet an affray
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to use or threatened unlawful violence towards

(A)_[another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THIRD PERSON..),]_
(B)_[other persons]_

and their conduct was such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3(1) and (7) of the Public Order Act 1986 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
aided / abetted / counselled / procured another
to use / threatened unlawful violence towards a third person / persons
and their conduct was such as would cause
a person of reasonable firmness to fear for personal safety

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A threat under this section cannot be made by words alone.
(ii) Where more persons have used or threatened unlawful violence etc (as above) than are charged, option (B) should always be used. See R v Mahroof (1989) at C119.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Three years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
